thread:
ops-bot: PAGE: P2 tenant-surge detected for tenant=sapphire-labs in dedicated-vpc-us-west-2. metric: queue_length > 1200 for 3m, tail_latency_p95 > 4s. paging oncall@eng-oncall
amelia (oncall): saw the page. I'm on it. pinging sapphire-sre and infra. any immediate customer reports?
sapphire-sre: customer says chat responses are timing out ~10-15s and some incomplete replies. They are on a single dedicated pool. Impacting a handful of production routes.
amelia (oncall): ok — initial hypothesis: lots of small requests causing batching inefficiency and queue buildup. could be max_batch_tokens or scheduler mis-profile for this tenant. Jay, can you look at the scheduler profile for sapphire-labs?
jay (scheduler): looking now. Their profile is using default-dedicated-v1: max_batch_tokens=1024, target_fill_ms=200, per-tenant-queue-size=250. For high QPS with short inputs, that lets big batches form and pins GPUs waiting for fills -> tail spikes.
amelia (oncall): understood. quick mitigations we can try: 1) lower max_batch_tokens to force smaller batches, 2) lower target_fill_ms so scheduler emits earlier, 3) isolate tenant queue throttle to cap in-flight. Which is lowest-risk quick change?
samir (infra): lowering target_fill_ms from 200 -> 50 is low-risk but may increase token overhead. Changing max_batch_tokens down to 256 is higher impact but should reduce p95. I can push a per-tenant override in the control plane now and revert.
amelia (oncall): go for target_fill_ms 50 and max_batch_tokens 512 as a first pass. apply one at a time and monitor. Can you also put a temporary ingress rate-limit to keep customer from overwhelming the pool? sapphire-sre — can you throttle at customer side or we do it server-side?
sapphire-sre: we can apply quick client-side throttle (we control the gateway) — will do 30% traffic drop for 10m while you tune.
amelia (oncall): thanks. samir, apply the scheduler override. show the command you run so we can audit.
samir (infra): running the per-tenant config change now:
```
curl -X POST "https://controlplane.internal/api/v1/tenants/sapphire-labs/overrides" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"scheduler": {"target_fill_ms": 50, "max_batch_tokens": 512}}'
```
samir (infra): response 202 accepted. on controller: deploy-id=deploy-enk5, rolling to pool dedicated-us-west-2
amelia (oncall): monitoring metrics: queue_length, p95_latency, gpu_util, tokens_per_batch. infra-bot will post updated charts in 60s.
infra-bot: Updated chart snapshot: https://dashboards.redwood/tenant/sapphire-labs?panel=queue_length (baseline -> spike -> after-change)
jay (scheduler): initial telemetry: token_per_batch dropped from 700 to ~320, p95 from 4.8s -> 2.2s within 40s. queue_length trending down from 1200 -> 300. good signal.
sapphire-sre: we still see occasional 5xx retries from gateway (rate limit), customers asking for ETA. I'll notify them it's being mitigated.
amelia (oncall): good. let's proceed to also set a temporary queue_shaper: max_inflight_requests=600 for the tenant so we don't saturate other tenants on the same host. Samir, apply that as well.
samir (infra): applied queue_shaper config via API:
```
PATCH /api/v1/tenants/sapphire-labs/config
{ "queue_shaper": { "max_inflight": 600, "burst_tolerance": 50 } }
```
samir (infra): queue_inflight dropped to 580, host load stable.
jay (scheduler): note — lowering max_batch_tokens further to 256 would cut p95 to ~1.4s in lab, but increases per-token cost ~8%. Recommend leave at 512 for now while customer does controlled rampdown.
amelia (oncall): agree. keep at 512. Samir, can you instrument a per-route fallback to smaller model if latency > 3s for 2 minutes? fallback mitigations might preserve UX for critical routes.
samir (infra): adding route-level fallback rule now. will take 90s to propagate.
ops-bot: Incident annotated: mitigation applied: target_fill_ms=50, max_batch_tokens=512, queue_shaper.max_inflight=600, route_fallback=true. Incident severity remains P2.
amelia (oncall): Sapphire SRE — can you confirm customer-visible latency? Also want their traffic pattern post-throttle.
sapphire-sre: confirmed: p95 observed at customer edge ~2.3s, error rate down from 3.2% -> 0.4%. Gateway throttle removed to 80% now, continuing slow ramp.
jay (scheduler): I'll open a follow-up PR to create a tenant profile template for customers with lots of short queries: short-reqs-optimized (target_fill_ms=40, max_batch_tokens=256, prefer_small_kvcache=true). We'll annotate cost tradeoffs.
amelia (oncall): nice. add a note to runbook line items 4-7: test in staging, run canary, apply with 2-min rollback window.
oncall-shift: handoff note: I'm taking over monitoring for the next 30m and will escalate if regressions. Amelia — want me to prepare a post-incident summary?
amelia (oncall): yes please, include timeline, commands run, metrics snapshots, and the PR link. Also schedule a meeting with Sapphire SRE tomorrow to discuss long-term profile and SLA implications.
sapphire-sre: appreciate the quick response. we'll be in the meeting. please include cost delta if we move to smaller batch profiles permanently.
amelia (oncall): will include cost delta estimate. ops-bot: closing the active page in 30m if no regression.
infra-bot: 15m telemetry check: queue_length stable ~120-320 range, p95 ~2.1s, GPU util steady 70%.
oncall-shift: marking incident as mitigated for now. assigning follow-up tasks: TICKET-3342 create tenant-profile-short-reqs, TICKET-3343 add runbook entry, TICKET-3344 schedule customer sync.
amelia (oncall): awesome team. final note: avoid changing both target_fill_ms and max_batch_tokens at once in prod next time unless we have a short rollback window — prefer one knob then observe. closing thread in 30m. :white_check_mark:
